statuses.description: A retained record from an actual AWS service call using synthetic data. The retained record proves only the bounded call and output that it contains.
Behavior executed in the local CareTrust runtime and covered by deterministic automated tests. It does not imply production deployment or independent interoperability.
A machine-readable contract or protocol-shaped artifact checked by automated tests. No deployed endpoint or end-to-end protocol exchange is implied.
Executable behavior limited to one local synthetic process or trust store. It does not establish an operational network or cross-organization result.
A documented field or concept mapping with no implemented exchange or conformance claim.
Design intent or future work for which no executable or contract-tested artifact is claimed.

capabilities.boundary: The retained live AWS record stops at an unverified draft and performs no review, activation, signing, authorization, or revocation.
The local claim lifecycle and deterministic policy do not establish production authorization or trust between independent organizations.
Revocation is enforced by an in-memory runtime registry. The checked record contract is not emitted or distributed by a durable status service.
No official HL7 validator, FHIR server, EHR, implementation guide, or independent FHIR implementation is used.
No OID4VC endpoint, credential issuance, valid presentation, wallet, holder binding, cryptographic verification, or conformance test runs.
Two synthetic entity identifiers resolve in one local process with caller-supplied statements and a pinned anchor; there is no network discovery, operational federation, or cross-organization test.
No HTTP server or deployed Phase 1 API is represented.

An authorized synthetic participating-organization user/client supplies CareTrust caregiver delegation/trust context; the caregiver does not query the holder. The synthetic data holder owns participant/client/user eligibility, patient matching, and final disclosure policy. No live HIE/EHR, MPI, SMART/OAuth, FHIR server, legal determination, or independent interoperability test is represented.
The dependency-free provider console replays generated synthetic artifacts in a browser. It is not a deployed case-management system, clinical chart, or measured workforce intervention.

The phone-sized caregiver client is a test/reference consumer over retained synthetic records. It stores presentation state only and makes no live identity-provider, API, EHR, HIE, or federation call.

The authorization-code, PKCE, OIDC, resource-indicator, and RAR exchange is a local synthetic harness. It does not connect to Login.gov or another production identity provider and does not establish production identity assurance.

One synthetic patient and multiple synthetic caregivers are evaluated in one local deterministic runtime. No live organization directory, credential registry, or production policy deployment is represented.

Intent, document, and application-requirements compilers emit source-linked drafts only. Human approval and deterministic policy remain separate; no compiler output can activate authority or return a permit.
No VC document, JSON-LD processing, VC securing mechanism, credential-status method, wallet, or VC conformance suite is implemented.
No FHIR authorization server, SMART scopes, launch context, EHR integration, or SMART conformance test is implemented.
